approved: Australian Transaction Reports and Analysis Centre Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy (Collection) Amendment Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record

This bill is part of a package that would replace the existing levy funding AUSTRAC's regulatory work with a broader industry contribution covering both its regulatory and financial intelligence functions.
The industry contribution would be set by the Minister for Justice via a legislative instrument, with the total amount capped at twice AUSTRAC's annual appropriation.
Around 900 larger reporting entities would pay the contribution, while about 3,000 smaller entities would be exempt.
Replaces the Supervisory Cost Recovery Levy with a new industry contribution that funds both AUSTRAC's regulatory and financial intelligence activities.
Limits the total industry contribution to twice the amount appropriated for AUSTRAC in a financial year.
Exempts approximately 3,000 reporting entities from paying the contribution, leaving about 900 larger entities to pay.
Reporting entities regulated by AUSTRAC, particularly larger ones that would pay the new industry contribution.

Defended the AUSTRAC supervisory levy bill as a necessary move to 100 per cent cost recovery given the fiscal mess inherited from six years of Labor government, and noted it requires an independent review of the industry contribution after the fourth anniversary of its commencement.

Reported that the Parliamentary Joint Committee on Human Rights had assessed 11 bills, found 10 did not require further scrutiny, deferred consideration of five and sought further information on the National Security Legislation Amendment Bill (No. 1) 2014, including its effects on specified human rights.
